newsitem.title: USA: ABN AMRO sees edge for Russia, Poland, Caspians.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO sees edge for Russia, Poland, Caspians.

text.p: Russia, Poland and former Soviet states in the Caspian region could edge out their Central and Eastern European neighbors in the ongoing competition for foreign investment, an ABN AMRO Bank official said on Tuesday.

Despite resistance to foreign control of its companies, Russia offers vast natural resources to entice foreign investment, said Theodoor Bark, ABN AMRO senior vice president and manager of corporate investment banking in Central and Eastern Europe, in an interview with Reuters.
"(Russia) will be able to attract foreign investors" even though "the Russians would like to be in control themselves," he said.
Bark compared the Russian economy to that of the United States about 100 years ago, when a few tycoons dominated business.

Industrial conglomerates modeled after those in South Korea and Japan are developing in Russia, Bark said. While these groups tend to shut out foreign investors, they may eventually allow joint ventures with some of their units, he said.
In addition, infrastructure improvements and cooperation with Asian neighbors should allow more foreign involvement in natural resource production in Russia's more remote regions, Bark said.

Turning to other countries, Bark said Poland would continue to attract large-scale foreign investment. He described the Polish economy as "westernized" and said privatization remained a major opportunity for foreigners.
Azerbaijan and other oil-rich Caspian-region states should also be leading targets of foreign investors, Bark said.
Asked about the recent poor performance of the Czech economy, Bark said he was not concerned.
"I do not worry about the Czech Republic," he said, adding that another round of privatizations should improve the economic picture.

On Tuesday, Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said he expected Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of "about zero percent" for the first quarter of 1997. Industrial output for the republic contracted in the first two months of the year.
Bark was in New York for an ABN AMRO conference on Central and Eastern Europe. He is based in Amsterdam.
